findings.reason: without an assertion that the peer session's scoring run is not reviewed, the gate proves only half the deliverable and passes on the half that matters least.
findings.text: §9's only assertion and negative control cover the resume arm ("Only the owning session's run is resumed, asserted through a stub launcher that records its calls"; control: "calling the sweep without the session resumes both"), yet the fixture is two runs "whose hold has lapsed" — a blocked run, which never reaches the scoring state the review reflex fires on (`dispatch_awaiting_reviews`, `reckon/crew/resumption.py:1888`) — so a node can satisfy the whole gate while the review reflex still dispatches a review onto an observed session's scoring run, the exact cross-session action the section exists to stop

findings.reason: a worker that implements the mechanism as written (filter the resume candidates, pass nothing to the reflex call) leaves the incident's own arm cross-session, so the repair would land on the wrong half of the path.
findings.text: the mechanism named is "pass the owning session and filter the candidate runs by it", which scopes only the sweep's `list_live` resume candidates, while the same sweep makes a second, independent pass — `dispatch_awaiting_reviews(project=project, config=config, launcher=launch)` (`reckon/crew/resumption.py:1888`) — that this section is named as part of the defect ("The same sweep also launches the review reflex, so an observing follower can review a peer's run as well as resume it") and that already accepts `session=` (`reckon/crew/recovery_review_acceptance.py:365`); the named mechanism does not reach it

findings.reason: the sentence is the one pointer §9 gives for the exact lines of the very code it just repointed, and a worker opening the map is sent to a file that no longer holds them; the sentence should name `reckon/crew_follow_commands.py` or record the map as stale.
findings.text: §9 says "The path map in the measurement plan §4 names the exact lines", but the map (`docs/research/data/monitor-scope-path-map.json`, question three) cites `reckon/cli.py:1633` (`def _sweep_lapsed_holds`), `:1641/1643` and `:1847` (`sweep(project)`), and `reckon/cli.py` is now 679 lines — the definition and cadence call live in `reckon/crew_follow_commands.py` (93/103 and the injected `sweep(project)` in `_sweep_quietly`), so the lines the map names no longer resolve

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — §9 asserts "The path map in the measurement plan §4 names the exact lines" (`:185-187`), but every line that map names for this sweep (`reckon/cli.py:1633/1641/1643/1847` in `docs/research/data/monitor-scope-path-map.json`) is in a `cli.py` that has since been split and is now 679 lines long.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — the node names one negative control and one assertion, both over the resume arm (`:197`, "through a stub launcher that records its calls"), while §9's own prose names the review-reflex arm as part of the defect; the gate can pass with the reflex still sweeping every session's runs.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the negative control is logged under the run directory, the plan's durable convention (§2/:50, §4/:75), never a scratchpad or node-local temp path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §9 introduces no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag into a symbol or path; `test_follow_sweep_is_session_scoped.py` is named by what it tests.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the stated mechanism ("pass the owning session and filter the candidate runs by it", `:183`) reaches only the sweep's resume loop, but the same sweep dispatches the review reflex from the project alone (`reckon/crew/resumption.py:1888`), which is the arm the section itself cites as the incident ("can review a peer's run as well as resume it").
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — the two halves (session-scope the follower's sweep, add the watcher's orphan sweep) are one change: scoping the follower creates the orphan gap the watcher fills, so neither half is separately closable.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §9 is declared `implementable` and is covered by the only open followup `f-tmstwiw-open-sections` ("Build the open monitor sections (§7–§12)"), it needs no `depends-on` edge because nothing must land first, and the sweep-ownership decision it rests on (`who-sweeps-an-unfollowed-session`) is locked in the decisions block.
